app.title: pH Diagrams: acid speciation explorer
app.summary: A person sets up to four acid dissociation constants and an acid concentration with sliders in the sidebar. The app works out how much of each protonation form of the acid is present across the whole pH scale. It draws the result in two charts side by side: one shows the fraction of each form, and the other shows the log concentration of each form against pH and pOH reference lines. The person moves the sliders and hovers over the curves to see where each form dominates, and can open a theory page with worked examples for acids with one, two and three dissociable protons.

task.text: Show how a polyprotic acid's forms are distributed across pH for the dissociation constants and concentration the person sets.

data.text: No data is loaded. The curves are computed from a few model parameters (up to four pKa values and one concentration) over a fixed pH grid from 0 to 14.
data.item: a protonation form of the acid (for example H2A, HA-, A2-), with its fraction and log concentration at each pH

stage.text: exploring acid-base equilibrium theory, as a teaching and reasoning aid

mechanism.text: Sliders in the sidebar set the pKa values and the concentration. Every change recomputes the fraction and log concentration of each form, and both linked line charts redraw side by side, with hover readouts for pH and value.

field.text: acid-base equilibrium speciation diagrams in analytical chemistry

workflow.name: tune a model's parameters and read the curves it predicts

steps.here: Four pKa sliders run from 0 to 14 in steps of 0.5. pKa1 starts at 1 and the others start at 0. A zero or out-of-order value cuts off that constant and every one after it, which sets how many protons the acid has.

steps.step: set the scale of the system
steps.here: A select slider picks the acid's analytical concentration from log-spaced steps between 1e-5 and 0.1.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: For each protonation form, the app computes the alpha fraction and log concentration at every pH step from 0 to 14, and names the forms as formulas (H2A, HA-, A2-).
Two charts redraw next to each other: the distribution diagram (α against pH) and the pC diagram (log C against pH, with dashed pH and pOH lines). Both are titled with the acid's general formula.
Hovering shows pH and α, or pH and logC. The chart toolbar adds spikelines and a hover mode, and allows zooming.
A theory page sets explanatory text beside fixed diagrams for an acid with one, two and three dissociable protons.

distinctive: The number of species is not chosen directly. It comes from how many pKa values are nonzero and in ascending order: invalid ones are dropped on purpose, for teaching.
The same computed speciation is shown two ways: as fractions that sum to one, and as log concentrations that depend on the acid concentration.
The log-concentration chart overlays the water lines (pH and pOH), so the crossings used in graphical acid-base reasoning are visible.
Species labels are chemical formulas with charges, generated from the number of protons.

parts.title: Parameter sidebar
parts.summary: Holds the sliders that set the acid's constants and concentration, and drives both diagrams.

parts.title: pKa sliders
parts.summary: Four sliders set the dissociation constants. Only the leading run of ascending values is kept, which sets how many protons the acid has.

parts.title: Concentration slider
parts.summary: Picks the acid's analytical concentration from log-spaced options, which shifts the curves in the log-concentration diagram.

parts.title: Side-by-side diagrams
parts.summary: Two columns show the distribution diagram and the pC diagram for the current acid, each titled with its formula.

parts.title: Distribution diagram
parts.summary: Plots the fraction (α) of each protonation form against pH from 0 to 14, with hover readouts.

parts.title: pC (log concentration) diagram
parts.summary: Plots the log concentration of each form against pH, with dashed pH and pOH reference lines and hover readouts.

parts.title: How to use and theory
parts.summary: A reading page that sets explanatory text beside fixed distribution and pC diagrams for example acids with one, two and three dissociable protons.
